children: BP PLC Sponsored ADR (LSE:BP.) is reshaping its portfolio—selling stakes in Tupinambá and Conifer to Shell while pursuing new production in Egypt and arbitration over LNG delays—amid takeover interest in U.K. North Sea assets, a raised analyst target and board changes ahead of 2027.
: BP agreed to sell 50% of Tupinambá (Santos Basin) and 30% of Conifer (Gulf of Mexico) to Shell, retaining operatorship and remaining stakes; deals pending regulatory approval and future drilling.
: EnQuest has shown interest in buying BP PLC Sponsored ADR (BP.)’s U.K. North Sea oil and gas assets; no deal terms or binding agreement have been announced.
: Piper Sandler raised BP PLC Sponsored ADR (BP.) price target to $46 from $43, reflecting an updated analyst valuation; no company actions, earnings, dividends, guidance, or transactions were noted.
: United Steelworkers Local 7-1 urged BP (BP.) to resume bargaining over the Whiting, Indiana refinery after a six-month shutdown, offering to meet with a federal mediator Sept. 14–15.
: BP PLC ADR (BP) joined arbitration and lawsuits against Venture Global over Calcasieu Pass LNG delays and alleged breach for selling cargoes into the spot market during high LNG prices
: BP (BP.) began production from Egypt's Fayoum-4 well, targeting about 80 million cubic feet per day of natural gas; company gave no operational timelines or financial details.
: BP (BP.) announced senior independent director Amanda Blanc will not seek re-election at the 2027 AGM as the board reviews commitments after Meg O'Neill became CEO in April.
